identification.notes: UR-protocol models (URTM*/SYWP* name prefixes) do not expose their service UUID as a constant in the app; identify them by advertised name prefix and enumerate services after connect. 0x1826 / 0xFFF0 cover the FTMS and FT classes respectively — 0xFFF0 is attributed to the FT proprietary protocol class ONLY. Whether UR-class pads advertise 0xFFF0 (or anything else) is unknown; their service and characteristic UUIDs must come from hardware capture, not from this list.

device.name: UREVO walking pad family (URTM*/SYWP* under-desk treadmills)
device.notes:
UREVO's walking pads / under-desk treadmills (model numbers seen in the app: URTM012, URTM018, URTM022, URTM023, URTM024, URTM029, URTM030, URTM041, SYWP006; retail families include SpaceWalk, Strol and CyberPad) are controlled over BLE by the official UREVO app (com.urevo.app). The manufacturer is alive and shipping; this is a cloud-independence spec: the app ties account, workout history, OTA and per-model metadata to the UREVO cloud (service.urevosports.com), while the control plane is local BLE GATT. No pairing/bonding or authentication strings exist anywhere in the treadmill code paths — control appears to be open to any central in range, as with other walking-pad brands.
The app's BLE layer (package:urevo_bluetooth) defines an EquipmentFactory that routes a discovered peripheral to one of several protocol classes. Three of them cover treadmills:
1. FTMS (FTMSEquipment/FTMSTreadmill) — standard Bluetooth Fitness
   Machine Service 0x1826. Selected when the advertisement carries
   0x1826. Characteristic set confirmed by the class's UUID getters:
   write 0x2AD9 (Control Point), notify 0x2ACD (Treadmill Data),
   0x2ADA (Fitness Machine Status) and 0x2AD3 (Training Status), plus
   reads of 0x2AD4 (Supported Speed Range) and 0x2AD5 (Supported
   Inclination Range). No vendor pre-amble or private characteristic
   exists in this path — treat it as plain FTMS 1.0.

2. FT proprietary (FTEquipment/FTTreadmill/FTBike) — private service
   0xFFF0, write 0xFFF2, notify 0xFFF1. Speaks the "BluePack A" frame
   grammar (below) with command class 0x44. Model-specific subclasses
   exist in the binary (FTTreadmill_5000/5002/5003/5004/51/5301/5302/
   5303/5304/5309/530A) selected from per-model config.

3. UR proprietary (UREquipment/URTreadmill) — UREVO's own treadmill
   protocol, matched by advertised-name prefix URTM* / SYWP* in
   EquipmentFactory.create. Speaks the same "BluePack A" grammar with
   command class 0x53, plus a second frame family "BluePack B"
   (0x5A 0xA5 header, >= 11 bytes) used at least for the controller
   version-info query. NOTA BENE: no GATT service/characteristic UUID
   constants exist in the binary for this class (verified 2026-08-12 by
   full string-table enumeration of libapp.so: the only 16-bit GATT
   UUIDs present are 0x180A, 0x1826, 0x2A23-0x2A29, 0x2ACD/2AD3/2AD4/
   2AD5/2AD9/2ADA, 0xFEE0-0xFEE2, 0xFFF0-0xFFF2) — the app binds the
   UR characteristics by GATT enumeration and/or per-model cloud config
   (DeviceConfig). The UR service/characteristic UUIDs must be captured
   from hardware (HCI snoop); do not guess them.

Relationship to KingSmith WalkingPad (see kingsmith-walkingpad.yaml): none at the protocol level. The KingSmith WiLink service 0xFE00, the ODM characteristic d18d2c10-… and the supplement service 24e2521c-… are all ABSENT from the UREVO binary (0 matches), and the UREVO frame grammar (02…03 + XOR-0x5A checksum; 5A A5 + CRC-16) shares nothing with WiLink (F7…FD + additive checksum). The only overlap is that both brands ship newer models speaking standard FTMS 0x1826.
The same app also drives UREVO recovery massagers (name prefix UCRM*; URRMEquipment/URRMEquipmentV2; services 0xFFF0 and 0xFEE0 — write 0xFEE2, notify 0xFEE1 on the V2 generation) and smart scales (WSEquipment; the hex string 55525753 = ASCII "URWS" appears in the factory matcher). Those product lines are out of scope for this spec.
SAFETY: motorised exercise equipment. The BluePack grammar carries no authentication, so anyone in radio range can issue start/speed commands once the frame bytes are confirmed against hardware.
Cloud dependency: none for control once the GATT endpoints are known. The UR class's reliance on cloud per-model config (DeviceConfig) for endpoint discovery is the one soft spot — capture the endpoints once and the cloud is no longer needed.

credentials.notes: BLE-only control plane; no credentials cross the link and no authentication of any kind was found in the treadmill classes.

factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset procedure is recoverable from the app binary for the treadmills (the massager classes have a RestoreFactorySettingsResponse, treadmills do not). The pads hold no network credentials and no bonds, so there is nothing to clear for local control. Not stated rather than guessed.

methods.description: Connect over GATT. FTMS models: standard FTMS flow (subscribe 0x2ACD/0x2ADA, write Control Point 0x2AD9). FT models: enable notify on 0xFFF1, write BluePack-A frames to 0xFFF2. UR models (URTM*/SYWP*): enumerate services, pick the write + notify characteristic pair, speak BluePack-A (class 0x53) frames.

steps.action: Power on the pad so it advertises.
Scan: name prefixes URTM* / SYWP* (UR protocol), advertised service 0x1826 (FTMS) or 0xFFF0 (FT proprietary).
Connect over GATT and discover services; pick the protocol class by advertised service UUID (0x1826 / 0xFFF0) or name prefix.
Enable notifications (0x2ACD/0x2ADA on FTMS, 0xFFF1 on FT, enumerated notify char on UR), then write commands (0x2AD9 / 0xFFF2 / enumerated write char).
steps.expect: Status notifications arrive; speed commands change belt speed. NOT yet confirmed on hardware.

setup.notes: No provisioning, pairing or bonding is visible in any treadmill code path of com.urevo.app v3.6.22: scan, connect over GATT, enable notifications and write commands. Confidence medium rather than high: this rests on static analysis only — no bonding/pairing API usage exists in the treadmill classes, but no hardware capture has confirmed the pads accept an unbonded central.

rejoin.notes: The pad joins no network. Any client may connect once the previous central disconnects (single-connection peripheral, as typical for this device class — not yet confirmed for UREVO hardware).

request_control.description: Standard FTMS Request Control (opcode 0x00). Assumed from FTMS 1.0; not yet confirmed as emitted by the app.

set_target_speed.description: Standard FTMS Set Target Speed (opcode 0x02), uint16-LE in 0.01 km/h. Assumed from FTMS 1.0; not yet confirmed as emitted by the app.

start_or_resume.description: Standard FTMS Start or Resume (opcode 0x07). Assumed from FTMS 1.0.

stop_or_pause.description: Standard FTMS Stop or Pause (opcode 0x08, param 0x01 stop / 0x02 pause). Assumed from FTMS 1.0.

characteristics.name: Treadmill Control Point
characteristics.notes: Write target for FTMS commands; responses parsed by FTMSControlResponse.onParseData (control-point response with result codes, per FTMS 1.0). Exact opcodes emitted by the app not yet extracted from the Dart AOT code — standard FTMS 1.0 opcode set expected (needs HCI snoop).

characteristics.name: Treadmill Data
characteristics.notes: Standard FTMS Treadmill Data; parsed by FtmsReadMixin. No vendor flag extensions found in the binary.

characteristics.name: Fitness Machine Status
characteristics.notes: Standard FTMS status events; in the class's notify-characteristic list.

characteristics.name: Training Status
characteristics.notes: In the class's notify-characteristic list (0x2AD3 = Training Status per FTMS 1.0).

characteristics.name: Supported Speed Range
characteristics.notes: Read by readSupportSpeedRange after connect; use it to bound speed commands per model.

characteristics.name: Supported Inclination Range
characteristics.notes: Read by readSupportInclinationRange; relevant on incline-capable models.

services.name: Fitness Machine Service (FTMS-generation models)
services.notes: Standard Bluetooth FTMS, selected by EquipmentFactory when the advertisement carries 0x1826 (class FTMSEquipment/FTMSTreadmill with FtmsReadMixin). The full characteristic set below is confirmed by the class's UUID getters in libapp.so v3.6.22 (each UUID string is referenced by the corresponding getter/reader method). No vendor extension, pre-amble or private characteristic was found in this path — unlike KingSmith's FTMS generation, there is no ODM characteristic and no supplement service. Command frames are built in code (no constant FTMS frames embedded); assume standard FTMS 1.0 Control Point semantics (0x00 Request Control, 0x02 Set Target Speed with uint16-LE 0.01 km/h, 0x07 Start/Resume, 0x08 Stop/Pause) until an HCI snoop confirms the exact opcode set the app emits.

characteristics.name: Status / response notifications
characteristics.notes: Inbound BluePack frames. Response model classes in the binary (package:urevo_bluetooth/src/model/response): TMStatusResponse, TMStartResponse, TMStopResponse, TMPauseResponse, TMSpeedConfigResponse, TMSlopeAndConfigResponse, TMVersionInfoResponse, TMMileageResponse, TMBlueStateResponse, TMSetSpeedAndSlopeResponse, TMGetDotMatrixScreenResponse / TMSetDotMatrixScreenResponse (models with a dot-matrix display), and BK*-mirrors for bikes (BKStatusResponse, BKConfigResponse, BKSportDataResponse, …). Per-field offsets inside these responses are not yet recovered — parsing lives in ResponseFactory. createResponse and the per-class parsers; needs an HCI snoop or further disassembly.

ft_prepared.description: FT class: prepare/ready the belt before a workout (FTEquipment.prepared).

ur_get_equipment_status.description: UR class: poll current equipment status — UREquipment.getEquipmentStatus, cmd 0x51 with NO sub-command byte. Answer is a TMStatusResponse.

ur_get_slope_config.description: UR class: query slope configuration — UREquipment.getSlopeConfig, cmd 0x50 sub 0x03. Answer is a TMSlopeAndConfigResponse.

ur_get_speed_config.description: UR class: query speed configuration (range/step) — UREquipment.getSpeedConfig, cmd 0x50 sub 0x02. Answer is a TMSpeedConfigResponse.

ur_set_speed_and_slope.description: UR class: set target belt speed and slope (UREquipment.setTargetSpeedAndSlope). Speed and slope are integer counts of the device-reported step (see service notes); slope 0 on flat models.

slope.description: Target incline in device slope-step counts; 0 on flat walking pads.

speed.description: Target speed in device speed-step counts (display speed / step). Absolute step TBD from the speed-config response.

ur_training_pause.description: UR class: pause, belt holds state (UREquipment.trainingPause).

characteristics.name: Command write
characteristics.notes:
All commands below are BluePack-A frames; checksums on the constant commands are shown resolved per the formula above. Every byte sequence here was recovered by disassembling the app's command builders (ARM, libapp.so v3.6.22) — none of it has been exercised against real hardware yet.
Known but NOT yet mapped (deliberately absent from the commands map because no emittable byte sequence is recovered): the UR class's controller version-info query, UREquipment.getControllerVersionInfo. It is built as a BluePack-B frame (5A A5 header, >= 11 bytes, CRC-16/CCITT involvement suspected), not BluePack A; its exact body is not yet extracted from the Dart AOT code. The answer parses as a TMVersionInfoResponse. Add it as a command only once the frame bytes are recovered (further disassembly or an HCI snoop).

services.name: BluePack proprietary service (FT class; UR class endpoint TBD)
services.notes:
Private 16-bit service 0xFFF0, write 0xFFF2, notify 0xFFF1 — the getters on FTTreadmill (get:serviceId / get:writeCharacteristicId / get:enableNotifyCharacteristicIds) reference exactly these UUIDs. This is the endpoint for the FT class (FTEquipment/FTTreadmill/ FTBike). The UR class (UREquipment/URTreadmill, name prefixes URTM*/SYWP*) speaks the SAME BluePack frame grammar (identical builder/serializer code, BluePackA.toUInt8List) but no UUID constants exist in the binary for it, so its GATT endpoints must come from hardware capture; the UR command set is documented here because the wire grammar is shared.
BluePack A frame grammar (both directions; recovered from BluePackA.toUInt8List / BluePackFactory.create / getCheckSum in libapp.so v3.6.22):

  02 <cmd> <sub> <payload...> <checksum> 03

- byte 0 = 0x02 (frame start; BluePackFactory dispatches on
  first == 0x02 AND last == 0x03)
- byte 1 = command class (0x44 FT equipment, 0x53 UR treadmill,
  0x50 config query, 0x51 status query; 0x40 also exists, purpose
  unidentified)
- byte 2 = sub-command / action (optional; absent on the 0x51
  status query)
- payload = zero or more parameter bytes - checksum = (cmd + sub + sum(payload bytes)) & 0xFF, then XOR 0x5A
  (disassembly of BluePackA.getCheckSum: additive sum of the command
  class, the sub-command and every payload byte, masked to 8 bits,
  XOR 0x5A)
- last byte = 0x03 (frame end)
A second frame family, BluePack B, starts 5A A5 and is at least 11 bytes long (BluePackFactory dispatch + BluePackB.fromUInt8List length check); the binary also contains a crc16CCITT routine (MSB-first, poly 0x1021). BluePack B is used at least by UREquipment.getControllerVersionInfo (which allocates a BluePackB). Its full layout and the CRC's exact coverage are not yet mapped.
Speed/slope encoding: UREquipment.setTargetSpeedAndSlope converts the display speed to wire counts as raw = display / speedStep, where speedStep comes from the unit/config helpers (the slope goes through the symmetric BlueNumExt fromSlope conversion). The absolute speed step (0.1 km/h or otherwise) is not pinned down by static analysis — read it from the 0x50 speed-config response on hardware.

services.name: Device Information Service
services.notes: Standard DIS, parsed by the app's BlueDIS class. Characteristic strings 0x2A23-0x2A29 (system ID, model number, serial number, firmware revision, hardware revision, software revision, manufacturer name) are all referenced by getters. The model-number string is the likely per-model key the app feeds into its config/factory routing.
